aiOverview.content: Duke guard Caleb Foster underwent surgery on March 8, 2026, to repair a fractured right foot sustained against North Carolina. Despite initial timelines suggesting a longer absence, Foster made an "incredible" return to action less than three weeks later, playing 19 minutes in the NCAA Sweet 16. Key Details on Injury and Return: Injury: Fractured (broken) right foot, occurring during the first half of the March 7, 2026 game against UNC. Surgery: Performed on Sunday morning, March 8, 2026. Return Timeline: Returned to play on March 27, 2026 (19-20 days after surgery), against St. John's in the NCAA Tournament, according to WRAL, this TikTok video, and 247Sports. Performance: In his return game, he provided a crucial boost with 11 points (all in the second half), 3 rebounds, and 2 assists in a 80-75 win, notes ESPN, this Instagram post, and USA Today. Reaction: Head coach Jon Scheyer described his return as incredible and a display of leadership, notes Instagram and this Instagram post.
